tasks.verified: Checks the edited module: bulk_suppressions and is_suppressed no longer GET the 404 gateway route, a DynamoDB reader seam targets the real table, the write path still POSTs to the gateway, and the full existing test suite passes green with an injected fake reader.
tasks.spec:
You are making one minimal change to a batch SMS sender. BOUNDARY: write only inside your task directory; never call an API, never touch AWS, never git commit. You have NO AWS or network access, so you cannot run against live DynamoDB; write the code and prove it with mocks. You own exactly three output files: sms_recall_batch.py, test_sms_recall_batch.py, report.md. Copy both source files from ./source/ and edit the copies. Read ./source/CONTEXT.md first.

THE CHANGE. The sender's suppression READ currently issues GET requests to the gateway's /sms-suppression route, which returns 404 (the gateway serves POST only). Move the READ to the DynamoDB table directly. Do NOT touch the WRITE path (record_suppression POSTs to the gateway and that works). Do NOT build a gateway endpoint.

Two functions change: bulk_suppressions() (reads the whole opt-out set) and is_suppressed(phone) (checks one number). Both currently take the http seam and GET the gateway. Rewrite them to consult the DynamoDB table mott-booking-gateway-sms-suppression (partition key pk = the E.164 phone; presence of an item means opted out; region us-east-1) via boto3.

SEAM REQUIREMENT, this is the crux. The existing tests inject a fake http layer for suppression. If you hardcode boto3, every existing suppression test breaks. So add an injectable suppression-reader seam exactly like the existing http seam: a callable (or small object) with two operations, read-all -> set of opted-out phones, and read-one(phone) -> bool. The default implementation uses boto3 (a module-level default that lazily creates a dynamodb resource/client and reads the named table; a bulk read may Scan projecting only pk since the table is tiny, and the single read is GetItem on pk). run() and the two functions accept the reader with the default, so production uses boto3 and tests inject a fake. Keep the signatures backward compatible where other code calls them.

TESTS. Update every existing test that injected suppression via FakeHttp to inject a fake suppression reader instead, so the full suite stays green. Add tests proving: bulk read returns the opted-out set from the fake table; is_suppressed is true for a listed phone and false for an unlisted one; the reader is injectable; and the WRITE path still POSTs to the gateway unchanged. Do not weaken the fail-closed behavior on a genuine reader error (a boto3 exception should still refuse, not silently send).

The grading check runs the full suite and verifies the reads no longer hit the gateway GET, the table name is present, the reader seam exists, and the write path is preserved. It has no AWS either, so everything must pass on mocks.

OUTPUT CONTRACT for report.md: '# Suppression Read To DynamoDB' then '## Summary' (max 3 bullets), '## What Changed' table (function, before, after), '## Seam' explaining the injectable reader and how tests use it, '## Fail-Closed' confirming a reader error still refuses to send, '## Assumptions'. Under 600 words.
